title: Number of Boomerangs
statement: `points` holds `n` distinct points of the plane, each written as `[x, y]`. Call an ordered triple of three different indices `(i, j, k)` a boomerang when point `i` is exactly as far (in straight-line distance) from point `j` as it is from point `k`. Order matters, so `(i, j, k)` and `(i, k, j)` are two separate boomerangs. Return how many boomerangs `points` contains.
notes:
## Intuition

The brute force tries every ordered triple, which is O(n³). Notice that a boomerang is decided by its first point `i`, the point both distances are measured from. Fix that pivot and sort the other points into groups by their distance to it. Any two different points from the same group, taken in either order, form a boomerang, so a group of size `c` contributes `c · (c - 1)` triples. Comparing squared distances keeps everything in exact integers.

## Approach

1. Set `total = 0`.
2. For each pivot `[x, y]`, build a fresh map `count` from squared distance to how many points sit at it.
3. For every point `[px, py]`, compute `distance = dx² + dy²` and add one to `count` for it. (The pivot itself lands at distance 0 alone and adds nothing.)
4. For each group size `same` in `count`, add `same · (same - 1)` to `total`.
5. Return `total`.

## Example 1, step by step

Points `[0,0]`, `[1,0]`, `[2,0]`.
- Pivot `[0,0]`: squared distances `0, 1, 4`; every group has size 1, adding 0.
- Pivot `[1,0]`: distances `1, 0, 1`; the group for `1` has size 2, adding `2 · 1 = 2`.
- Pivot `[2,0]`: distances `4, 1, 0`; adds 0.

`total` is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each pivot measures its distance to every point once.
- Space: O(n): the map for one pivot holds at most `n` distances.

## Pitfalls

- Count ordered pairs: a group of size `c` gives `c · (c - 1)`, not `c · (c - 1) / 2`.
- Use squared distances; `Math.sqrt` can produce slightly different floats for equal distances.
- Reset the map for every pivot; distances only match when they share the same first point.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total` | boomerangs counted so far |
| `x`, `y` | the pivot point, the first point of the triple |
| `count` | squared distance from the pivot → number of points at it |
| `px`, `py`, `dx`, `dy` | another point and its offset from the pivot |
| `distance` | squared distance from the pivot |
| `same` | size of one distance group |
